title: Az-Zahir, the Manifest
hookLine: the Manifest, evident in all His signs (57:3)
tomorrow: hidden because He's far away, or because He's too close?

cards: Old riddle: what's in plain sight all day and still can't be seen? Here's a stranger one, straight from the Qur'an.
The verse from the last two days goes on, in Pickthall's words: "He is the First and the Last, and the Outward and the Inward." Outward and Inward. Manifest and Hidden.
Opposites, side by side, about the same One. So which is it? Is God obvious, or hidden?

teach.b: The verse's answer is both, about different things. Today's Name takes the first half. Az-Zahir, the Manifest, the Outward.
A du'a of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Sahih Muslim says: You are the Outward, and there is nothing above You. Outward how?
Through what the Qur'an calls signs, ayat, the same word it uses for its own verses. Some signs are huge: the sky, the turn of night and day. And one list of signs is easy to read past.
"And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours." Read that again.
Right after the heavens and the earth: the different ways people talk, and the different shades of their skin. Not a problem to fix. A sign.

teach.h: MADE DIFFERENT, TO KNOW ONE ANOTHER.
teach.b: Another verse says why the differences are there: "O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another."
One human family, made different on purpose, so its people would have to get to know each other.
So here's half the puzzle solved: God is outward in what He made, including the face across the lunch table that looks nothing like yours. Tomorrow, the Inward.

how: Muslims recite 57:3 and the Prophet's du'a that names the First, the Last, the Outward and the Inward, and speak of reflecting on Allah's signs, ayat, in creation and in people.

o: the Well-known, whose name all people know
the Visible, whom eyes can plainly see
the Manifest, evident in all His signs

games.q: what's inside the riddle — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an treats differences of language and color as a problem
it calls them His signs, and says nations and tribes were made to know one another.
one verse calls Allah both the Outward and the Inward
"the Outward and the Inward; and He is Knower of all things."
Az-Zahir means God can be seen with the eyes
the Outward is evident in His signs; the same verse also calls Him the Inward.

games.q: a new kid at school has an accent, and someone at lunch imitates it for laughs. what would the verse of languages and colors say about that accent?
o: it's one of God's signs; the Qur'an counts languages among them.
light teasing is fine; accents are just funny sometimes.
help him lose it quickly so he fits in with everyone else.
games.why: the Qur'an lists the difference of your languages and colors right after the heavens and the earth, as signs, and says people were made different to know one another.

practice: Look at your own hand for the whole sit: its lines, its color, the way it moves the moment you ask it to. The Qur'an counts signs within ourselves too. Let your hand be one, in plain sight all day, and seen now.

wordCard.voice: Az-Zahir. The Manifest, the Outward: evident in all His signs, from the sky to the many languages of people.

orig.note: Arabic: the Manifest, the Outward. paired with al-Batin in 57:3.

carryVoice: For the road: manifest, in the sky, in your hand, and in every accent you heard today. Half the riddle, solved.
